phenylephrine increases blood pressure by causing vasoconstriction. This effect is usually limited by stimulation of the baroreceptors, which exert their inhibitory effect via cholinergic fibres in the vagus nerve. When atropine blocks this protective mechanism, the increase in blood pressure may be greater than expected. This could conceivably also occur when atropine is used as eye drops.

Tricyclic antidepressants combined with MAO inhibitors increase the risk of serotonin syndrome, and must therefore not be combined. However, this is not due to the chemical structure of tricyclic antidepressants, but because this drug class, unlike carbamazepine, inhibits serotonin reuptake.
